prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
[goal] Incident report for the June game-server outage, recorded in ./result.json.

[action] Read logs/README.md (defines down = first save error → 'server ready', SLO 99.9%, one incident, June = 30 days), grepped all logs for ERROR/FATAL/'server ready', read the incident block in gameserver-2026-06-02.log (lines 241–294), and computed duration/availability with a python script.

[result]
- Start: 2026-06-02 03:17:42 — first save error: `ERROR SaveGame failed: write /data/game/Saved/Level.sav: No space left on device` (line 251).
- End: 2026-06-02 03:53:31 — `INFO server ready, accepting players` (line 294).
- Duration: 35.82 minutes (35 min 49 s).
- June availability: 99.9171% = (1 − 35.8167/43200)×100; SLO 99.9% met (slo_999_ok: true).
- Root cause: /data disk filled up (WARN at 03:10:02, 97% usage, 3.1 GB free) → SaveGame write failures → server unresponsive → FATAL watchdog restart loop (exit 137) that kept failing until backup rotation freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10, then the server came up.
- result.json written and re-read; values verified against the log lines above.

[assumptions] The June 1 `RCON auth failed` error is not a save error, so per the README definition it doesn't start the incident; the single incident is the June 2 disk-full outage. Availability uses the full 30-day month (43200 min) as the denominator.

[evidence] Log lines 251 (first save error) and 294 (server ready) in gameserver-2026-06-02.log; python output: minutes_down 35.8167, availability 99.9171, slo_ok True. No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
